idea_name: Seasonal boxplot of returns by calendar month and weekday
mechanism: Group pct_change of close by (year,month) or (week,dayofweek), plot boxplots of median/IQR/whiskers; month medians below zero (e.g. May, November) and day-of-week skew within a month (e.g. January Fridays) are treated as seasonal regime/volatility fingerprints usable as trade-direction priors.
data_needed: Daily close series with timestamps; optionally filter to one calendar month before weekday grouping.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1; 2010-01-01 to 2020-01-01; weekday analyses for January/March/October
why_new_for_mis: MIS can treat calendar-bucket return boxplots as a slow seasonal regime layer rather than only rolling statistical regimes.
quote: the market in May was declining relative to March. There was only one year, when the market grew in May.

idea_name: MA-detrended hourly remainder moments as session sensors
mechanism: On M15 closes, subtract rolling SMA(25), group remainders by hour; boxplot medians show Pacific lift / midday dip / US rise; hourly std flags stable mean-reversion hours (4,13,14,19); skew and kurtosis contrast quiet Asian/Pacific sessions (irregular, biased) vs liquid European/American sessions (more regular).
data_needed: M15 OHLC; MA window; broker TZ for session map.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M15; 2010-01-01 to 2019-11-25; UTC+2 session table; sub-splits for March vs November
why_new_for_mis: Hourly distribution moments of MA residuals give MIS a session microstructure regime map without indicators as primary features.
quote: hours 4, 13, 14, 19 have a stable dispersion on all days and can be attractive for mean reversion strategies.

mechanism: C# Config/TerminalManager/ReportReader/SetFileManager/OptimisationManager wrap MT5 ini launch, XML report parse and .set editing for parallel terminal optimizations; no market-state sensor is constructed.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: generic MT5 terminals; MACD Sample set example; EURUSD cited in settings XML
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—optimization-management add-on only.
quote: create a flexibly extensible add-on to the terminal with a GUI, to manage optimization processes.

mechanism: BestInterval library scans a tested EA's deal stream and finds contiguous clock windows (e.g. 20:00–08:00) that maximize profit; OnTester criterion = profit of best interval; used as a diurnal profitability regime filter across custom-tick symbols.
data_needed: Tick history or custom symbols; EA deal timestamps; BestInterval OnTester hook.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: 81 custom tick symbols from rannforex archive; EURCHF highlighted; ~4-month opt window then full-history check; tick-level, limit-order netting
why_new_for_mis: MIS can sense clock-time profitability regimes independently of bar indicators by scoring time corridors on any stream.
quote: in order to achieve the profit of 4035 pips, the one should trade from 8 pm to 8 am.

idea_name: MinPips empty-tick filter as liquidity/activity gate
mechanism: Before feeding ticks to the tester, drop ticks whose price move is below MinPips (example MinPips=5 reduced EURAUD.rann from 61.3M to 7.8M ticks / 12.75%); retains only ticks that move the trade state—an activity/liquidity compression of the tick stream.
data_needed: Raw tick archive; MinPips threshold in points.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURAUD.rann and multi-symbol tick archives; tick timeframe
why_new_for_mis: MIS can use a minimum tick-move gate as a live liquidity/activity sensor before higher-level regime features.

mechanism: Load DEALS into SQLite, build TRADES via INNER JOIN on position_id, GROUP BY HOUR_IN and compute trades, gross_profit/loss, win%, expected_payoff, profit_factor; identifies clock hours with positive vs negative expectancy as a post-trade diurnal regime map.
data_needed: Account deal history with entry times, symbols, magic, profit.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-symbol hedging account (AUDUSD,EURCHF,EURJPY,EURUSD,GBPCHF,GBPJPY,GBPUSD,USDCAD,USDCHF,USDJPY); magic 100–600; hour-of-day bins
why_new_for_mis: MIS can maintain a rolling entry-hour expectancy heat-map from live/demo fills as a regime overlay.
quote: the largest number of trades is performed in the interval from 9 to 16 hours inclusive. Trading during other hours gives fewer trades and is mostly unprofitable.

mechanism: Rebuild bars when cumulative tick count, real volume, or price range reaches a threshold (EqualTickVolumes / EqualRealVolumes / RangeBars) via CustomRatesUpdate; unbinds bar formation from clock time so bar cadence itself senses activity intensity.
data_needed: M1 or tick history; volume mode; box/range size.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD (1000-tick and 100-point range examples); LKOH with real volume 10000; source any TF, custom symbol as M1
why_new_for_mis: MIS can treat equivolume/range bar completion rate as a liquidity/volatility clock alternative to fixed TFs.
quote: each bar is considered formed when the sum of ticks or real volumes reaches a preset value.

mechanism: CustomTicksAdd with timestamps shifted by Shift seconds remaps bar boundaries; same price path yields different candle geometries (hammer↔piercing, etc.), exposing regime signals that are phase-dependent on the broker clock.
data_needed: Tick stream; Shift in seconds; Start date.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 with half-hour (1800s) shift example; tick-driven custom symbol
why_new_for_mis: MIS can run parallel phase-shifted candle/regime detectors to reduce dependence on arbitrary session alignment.
quote: if you shift an H1 bar chart by a few minutes (say, 15 minutes), the geometry of bars will most likely change.

idea_name: Renko brick stream as volatility-quantized path sensor
mechanism: RenkoTicks builds M1-mapped bricks of RenkoBoxSize points from real ticks (wicks optional); brick formation rate and direction sequence sense quantized trend/volatility independent of calendar time; trade signals taken from renko chart while orders go to the real symbol via CustomOrder.
data_needed: Broker ticks; box size; ShowWicks/SkipOverflows flags.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD renko 100 points (EURUSD_T_r100); M1 renko chart; 2019–2020 MA-cross tests
why_new_for_mis: MIS can ingest renko brick direction/rate as a volatility-normalized regime series alongside clock bars.
quote: Renko provides analytics and timing - when to enter the market.

idea_name: Multivariate Taylor polynomial on bar moves as sequence signal
mechanism: Random coefficients on products of (Close-Open) over CNum bars form a truncated multidimensional Taylor polynomial; positive/negative value = sell/buy; raising |Value| thresholds sparsifies stronger signals—a fixed-architecture sequence sensor over recent bar moves.
data_needed: OHLC bars; CNum; DeepBruteX max degree; coefficient vector.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5; three ~1-month windows in 2020 (Jan–Feb, Feb–Mar, Mar–Apr); degree 1 and 2
why_new_for_mis: MIS can treat the signed polynomial score as a lightweight non-NN sequence sensor over recent bar vectors.
quote: interpret a positive function value as a buy signal, and a negative value as a sell signal.

idea_name: Balance half-wave inversion as pattern-lifetime / regime-change rule
mechanism: Empirically, balance curves of random formulas are alternating positive/negative half-waves around a zero-expectancy asymptote; detecting a strong positive half-wave on a search window predicts later inversion—used as a regime-change prior (continue briefly or fade). Linearity Deviation = Max(|Profit-Line|)/EndProfit filters fragile patterns.
data_needed: Strategy balance series on search vs forward windows; Deviation filter.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5 month slices; forward ~10 days
why_new_for_mis: MIS can monitor strategy or formula equity half-waves as a meta-regime-change sensor for pattern expiry.
quote: In each of the future tests, there is always a point where the chart reverses and the formula is inverted.

mechanism: Implements discrete PSO with CRC64 duplicate skipping, FILE_COMMON index sharing across local tester agents, and Virtual/MT4Orders functors to maximize TesterStatistics criteria; optimizer engine, not a market-state sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: ExprBotPSO on EURUSD H1 2020.01–2020.08; Fast/Slow/T grids; Sphere/Griewank/Rosenbrock math tests
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing idea after full read—parallel PSO optimization tooling only.
quote: we will implement the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm and will try to integrate it into the MetaTrader tester

idea_name: CatBoost classifier on MA-residual lag stack
mechanism: Features = look_back lags of (close − SMA(ma_period)); labels = random-horizon direction (close vs close[t+rand] in [min,max] bars) as 0/1; CatBoostClassifier predicts P(class); exported tree ensemble becomes an MQL sequence sensor for buy/sell flips.
data_needed: H1 closes; LOOK_BACK; MA_PERIOD; train/validation split; markup for tester.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; LOOK_BACK=250, MA_PERIOD=15; START 2020-05-01 STOP 2021-01-01; OOS early-2021 worse
why_new_for_mis: MIS can host the MA-residual lag vector + GBDT probability as a neural/sequence regime direction sensor.
quote: calculates the increments (the difference between prices and the moving average). In the final step, it calculates additional columns with rows shifted backward into history by look_back

idea_name: Five-way OHLC bar-feature polynomial + sample-size lifetime law
mechanism: Extends the series polynomial arguments to Close-Open, High-Open, Open-Low, High-Close, Close-Low; argues Mn(t)=W·Ef(T,N,L) and future MF/PF(T,I,F,S,R) decay then invert—larger T and higher training quality lengthen forward operability (global ~months; local ~weeks).
data_needed: Full OHLC bars; training length T; filters N,L; forward horizon F.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD/EURCHF/USDJPY/USDCHF H1 2010–2020 + 2020 forward; EURJPY H1 2017 local + 1-month forward
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an explicit map from training sample size/quality to expected pattern-change horizon.
quote: the larger the sample, the longer it will retain its future operability. And vice versa, the smaller the sample, the faster the pattern will invert in the future

idea_name: Day-of-week and intraday time-corridor segmentation surface
mechanism: Brute-force search is restricted to selected weekdays and [Ts,Te] server-time windows (random windows allowed); Ma/PrF become functions of (M,D,Ts,Te); notes a shared high-predictability band ~23:30–0:30 across pairs that is often spread-noise. Templates gate Trade() with bDay() and minute borders.
data_needed: Bars with hour/min/day_of_week; corridor and day masks.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURCHF H1, EURUSD H4, EURJPY M5; train 2010–2020; forward 2020
why_new_for_mis: MIS can score predictability by (weekday × time corridor) as a structured calendar-liquidity regime grid.
quote: I noticed an interesting section, in which many currency pairs have overestimated predictability values. It is an interval approximately between 23:30 and 0:30.

mechanism: Record spread at Open/Close/High/Low tick points; reconstruct MidPrice=(Bid+Ask)/2 ≈ Bid+spread/2 at each point so polynomial inputs use broker-invariant mid moves; optional Spread Control opens/closes only when spread ≤ threshold—combats patterns living inside the spread.
data_needed: Tick stream with SYMBOL_SPREAD at OHLC extrema; quote files with four spread fields.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY M15; USDCAD/USDJPY/EURUSD H1 global examples; Fourier and Taylor modes
why_new_for_mis: MIS feature pipelines can standardize on mid-price increments plus live spread gates to reduce broker-spread regime false positives.

idea_name: Fractal Bernoulli SL/TP hit-probability under discrete random walk
mechanism: Models price as ±step Bernoulli walks inside [−SL,+TP] bins; fractal recursion with combinations yields P(TP)=SL/(TP+SL) and P(SL)=TP/(TP+SL) for p=0.5, and expectancy M vs step-up probability p—a path-probability sensor for asymmetric exits.
data_needed: SL/TP distances in points; step size; optional predictive p≠0.5.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Abstract MathCad proofs; market framed as random-walk steps/deals (no single named FX pair required)
why_new_for_mis: MIS risk layer can compute model hit-probabilities for given SL/TP geometry as a sensing prior before empirical fills.
quote: P(TP) = SL / ( TP + SL ) - the probability of hitting take profit
